text:
incident-bot: Pager duty: reserved-pool alert triggered for resv-us-east-1 — utilization 96% and sustained throttle events. paging oncall @maria @devon. link: https://alerts.redwood/internal/4523456000 :rotating_light:

pager-duty: 🔔 Severity: P1 — Dedicated reserved GPU pool saturation. Queue growth > 3x, customer throttles reported. Please join bridge: https://bridge.redwood/4523456000 (meet now)

maria: I'm on it, joining bridge. @devon @priya can you triage autoscaler + reservation telemetry?

devon: looking. quick check: autoscaler is generating scale requests but cloud API returns 429s. digging into autoscaler logs now.

devon: logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:03Z autoscaler scale_request id=abc123 status=429 reason=RateLimitExceeded
requested_nodes=4 created_nodes=0 pool=resv-us-east-1
2026-03-15T02:14:18Z autoscaler retry_attempt=1 status=429
```

priya: confirmed queue backlog for reserved pool. Most affected tenants: AcmeHealth (reserved ID resv-ACM), NovaBank (resv-NOV). Prefix cache hit low due to long sessions, KV caches ballooning.

evAN: (on call) NovaBank is reporting 503s from their app, they're pinging support. I put them on hold while we triage. @account-team fyi.

maria: opening incident bridge and tagging CS. bridge up: https://bridge.redwood/4523456000 — invite sent to acct leads.

account-team: joined. NovaBank asked for ETA. Can we give a short window?

maria: short window estimate: if we can provision burst nodes from shared pool and/or manually evict noisy tenant sessions we should relieve pressure in ~8-12 minutes. working on both in parallel.

devon: we see two failure modes: 1) cloud provider throttling autoscaler API requests (429) causing scale to stall, 2) noisy tenant sessions causing per-GPU saturation even if nodes exist. We need immediate burst and targeted eviction.

devon: issuing manual burst add to reserved pool (requires infra override). running:
```bash
# idempotent CLI
rctl pool add-burst resv-us-east-1 --count 4 --reason "pager: emergency burst" --expires 60m
```

support-bot: Approval required from infra-ops. @devon request sent to infra-ops.

devon: infra-ops approved via quick channel. proceeding. provisioning started.

support-bot: burst add accepted. provisioning logs show instance requests submitted to cloud provider.

priya: while nodes come up, we should evict the largest noisy session groups. list top tenants by GPU-usage: silo-772 (noisy), batch-test (dev), resv-ACM (AcmeHealth critical). Recommend evicting silo-772 first.

maria: agree. eviction command:
```
orch evict --tenant silo-772 --force --reason "noisy neighbor mitigation" --min-remaining 2
```

devon: eviction started. telemetry shows immediate drop in GPU utilization on 2 nodes.

support-bot: burst nodes have entered Provisioning -> Ready state. New GPUs available, autoscaler will rebalance pods.

priya: autoscaler now seeing capacity and scheduling backlogged work. queue length decreasing from ~12k -> ~3.1k in 6 minutes.

evan: update from NovaBank: error rate down from 7% -> 1.2%, some retries still failing but much better. AcmeHealth still seeing throttles on heavy generation routes (long sequence lengths).

maria: quick customer impact summary for bridge notes:
- AcmeHealth: sustained throttling on long-gen endpoints, estimated affected requests ~30% of peak over last 25m.
- NovaBank: partial degradation, peak 7% errors, now reduced to 1-2%.
- Internal SLA risk: reserved-pool latency SLO breached for ~18m.

devon: root cause hypothesis: cloud provider rate-limited repeated autoscaler API calls (backoff insufficient), causing delayed provisioning. Meanwhile a heavy noisy tenant (silo-772) consumed disproportionate GPU memory and compute, exacerbating queue growth.

priya: mitigation applied: manual burst + targeted eviction. follow-ups: implement exponential backoff + jitter in autoscaler, increase per-account burst quota, and add tenant-level soft caps to avoid single-tenant saturation.

maria: I've created incident ticket INC-2026-4523 and linked live logs: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-4523. Assigning to devon/priya for immediate postmortem items.

account-team: notified AcmeHealth and NovaBank. NovaBank wants a post-incident writeup and root-cause timeline.

support-bot: created support case 12345 for NovaBank and 12346 for AcmeHealth. Tickets attached to INC-2026-4523.

devon: quick mitigation checklist saved to runbook:
- bump burst (rctl pool add-burst)
- evict noisy tenant (orch evict)
- if autoscaler 429s persist, route new scale requests through proxy with consolidated batching

priya: leaving notes for SRE: add alert for sustained cloud-autoscaler 429 rate > 5/min and queue growth > 2x baseline. Also add tenant-level telemetry export for top-10 GPU consumers.

maria: handing off monitoring and follow-up to devon (overnight). I'll update the oncall rotation and make sure CS gets the postmortem. devon?

devon: taking handoff. current state: pool util down to 72%, queue length trending to normal, noisy tenant evicted and flagged for review. I'll own the postmortem and remediation PRs.

maria: thanks team. closing bridge in 10. final note: create retrospective with timeline, customer comm drafts, and proposed autoscaler fixes. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: incident bridge closed by maria.

maria: last message for handoff: summary for oncall notes -> cause: autoscaler rate-limit + noisy tenant; mitigations: manual burst + eviction; customer impact: AcmeHealth moderate (30% throttles), NovaBank partial (brief 7% errors); follow-ups assigned to devon/priya.

devon: acknowledged. I'll post a runbook PR and start the postmortem doc.

maria: handing off. good job everyone. :tada:
